results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 61 outline summaries match the controlling idea of the aligned spec paragraph, in spec order.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Kestrel & Pine: The Card-Testing Night ¶5
results.quote: In March 2027 Noor Visser, Head of Engineering since January, reads the incident report for the Waypoint program and asks a different question
results.finding: The outliner needed two phrases (why SCA did not fire and the ad hoc fix / Noor's reframing). Unlike the other two-part unit (Account Takeover ¶3, which opens with an umbrella sentence), this paragraph has no sentence tying the failed defence to the question it left, so it reads as two ideas.
Account Takeover, Bots and Scraping ¶3 was marked, but its opening sentence ('The cart and the catalog are the other doors bots use') unifies hoarding and scraping as the spec declares.
Every unit supports one of S1-S5 or the introduction/conclusion functions.

results.draft_locus: Card Data: Where PCI DSS Draws Its Line ¶6
results.quote: ("Adyen is solely responsible for the security of cardholder data only as soon as Adyen receives the data", Adyen docs, n.d.)
results.finding: The Adyen quotation sits in parentheses after the attestation clause with no sentence saying what it shows (that the merchant stays responsible until the PSP receives the data); flow reader A re-read to see what it supported.
Other evidence items (Imperva statistic, vendor quotations, BA, Polyfill, CosmicSting, PCI dates, tables and figures) are introduced and their point stated.

All other transition_in boundaries express the declared relationship and pick up the carried-over information.

Opens on a puzzling scenario (the checkout accepting strangers), states the stakes with BA, the merchant's share, Eva's order and a roadmap.
Opens by answering Noor's question, sorts what is established, contextual and the author's judgement, ends with questions and a hand-off.
¶1 joins the doors into one gap (open by design, told apart only by the decline rate and owned inventories) and states what a merchant can then do.
Returns to Noor's question and to Eva's iDEAL payment beside one of the 48,000 attempts.

The reader names card testing (OAT-001), explains why the certification and an IP block do not help, and gives the control ladder, decline-rate alert, kill switch, no retries, runbook and the response steps (cancel orders, rotate keys).

The reader places hosted fields in SAQ A subject to eligibility and the acquirer, explains 6.4.3/11.6.1 and the SAQ A statement, lists inventory, CSP, SRI and tamper detection, 12.8 and 8.4.2. It omits that a custom form moves the merchant to SAQ A-EP or D, which the chapter contains (minor).

The reader gives enforced MFA, no shared accounts, named agency accounts, leavers removed, one identity and restricted key per integration with an owner in a vault, rotation, app scope review, and why (admin bypasses everything, ownerless keys force rotating everything). Webhook signatures are not mentioned (minor).

The intro reader predicts the sections in order, the no-break-in framing, the merchant's share and scope exclusions, Eva and the 48,000 attempts, and evidence from the Kestrel & Pine case, BA, PCI requirement numbers and vendor statements. It places 6.4.3/11.6.1 in the PCI section rather than the skimmer section (minor).
